tasks.objective: Deliver every requested item to its place on its destination board, seated, released and still. How the robots share the work is your choice.
rules: Deliver the three requested source-identity items to each destination board. Station IDs identify inventory and destination orders, not exclusive robot ownership.

Transfers may be direct airborne handovers or safe stable tabletop staging. There are no marked or mandatory intermediate regions, predefined buffer positions, prescribed routes or fixed transfer pairs. The planner chooses whether to wait, stage or hand over. Establish receiving support before releasing an airborne item.

Each final position shows the required color and shape: a square for a cube and a circle for a cylinder, 1.4 times the object width or diameter. These are visual identity cues, not enlarged acceptance tolerances. Slot numbers and source identities disambiguate orders.

L1: release stably at the final board targets. L2 and L3: both flat blades must enter the real blind slots and the item must be released, seated and stable. L2 has a fixed board; L3 has the same three inline sockets on a passive spring-supported z/roll/pitch board. Preserve prior placements and allow gripper opening and withdrawal clearance.

Cubes have 60 mm sides; cylinders have 60 mm diameter and height. Blades initially point up or sideways. Grasp, airborne reorientation, receiving grasp and subsequent insertion must form a feasible continuous sequence. Allocation, routes and independent concurrent work are planner choices; minimize unnecessary cycling, staging and regrasping while maintaining real support and collision clearance.
Only robot actuators and real contacts may affect the live task. No hand welds, object state writes, resets, hidden state tools or runtime physics edits.

tasks.objective: Build the target pattern: one released cube in every cell, in the color the pattern gives. How the robots share the work is your choice.
rules: Build the supplied Tulip pattern, background cells included: one released cube in each cell.

Cube side is 60 mm and common cell-center pitch is 71 mm. L1 has 70 mm clear square pockets, L2 3 mm red printed lines, L3 no visible grid. The four colors are cream, navy, coral and sage. The target image matches world north-up, centered on the declared assembly origin.
Stock allocations do not restrict which robot can use an item. Preserve completed placements and account for finger release/withdrawal clearance.
Only robot actuators and real contacts may affect the live task. No hand welds, object state writes, resets, hidden state tools or runtime physics edits.
The pattern matrix and the reference image are already in world orientation (row 1 north, column 1 west); use them as given.

tasks.objective: Carry every timber to GOAL with at least one airborne handover each, and release it there. How the robots share the work is your choice.
rules: Move all 2 numbered payload assemblies from their individual initial positions toward the common GOAL. START marks the route origin; returning scattered payloads to START is not required.
Route regions and arrows indicate progress. Grasp points, handover locations, robot teams, allocation and execution order are planner choices. Independent work may run concurrently.

Carrying a timber in the air takes at least two arms holding it. Every timber must have at least one qualified airborne handover (below); the receiving team may keep an arm that already holds it. Establish the receivers' hold before a sender lets go.
Grasp the red timber, not a pendant, ring or shaft. Keep the whole assembly clear of table and floor during airborne transport, except for the allowed final GOAL landing.
Any final placement in GOAL is allowed, including timbers touching or stacked on each other.

Each timber must have at least 70 percent of its centreline length in the vertical space above the GOAL outline. Final completion requires release from every robot; direct or indirect table support is not required.
Only ordinary robot actuators and real contacts may change the live task. No hand welds, object-state writes, hidden-state tools, runtime physics changes or stabilizing attachments.

A handover qualifies only while the timber is off the table and at least two current holders keep it: a new arm must hold the timber for at least 0.2 seconds before a current holder lets go. A timber placed in GOAL without a qualified handover is not complete; a regrasp of a timber resting on the table is never a handover.

A timber that falls may be lifted again by the arms that held it when it fell. If any other arm picks it up, none of that timber's handovers counts until it is put down, lifted again by those arms and handed over again in the air. Pushing or dragging a timber along the table is allowed but is never a handover.
Collisions, drops and other process events are recorded separately. Recover using ordinary robot actions; do not reset, respawn or erase history.

tasks.objective: Unlock the code: find the correct nonzero input and hold it on every dial at once, using only the BEST record as feedback. How the robots share the work is your choice.
rules: The face has 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 at 60-degree intervals. Each private password digit is 1..5; 0 is an invalid initial position. Clockwise labels 4 and 5 may be reached as -120 and -60 degrees; +180 and -180 are the same mark 3.

BEST starts at 0 and shows the largest correct-count achieved by any one complete valid input in this episode. It is not the current correct-count. An unchanged record can mean equal or worse; never combine per-dial results from different attempts.

READY is grey when the current input is invalid, amber while qualifying and green after every dial is within 4 degrees of a nonzero mark, actually grasped, and stable for 0.25 seconds. Green means a valid input, not a correct password.

The BEST digit is bright only when READY is green. Otherwise its retained value stays visible in dim grey-brown, including while the amber lamp is qualifying. Brightness does not change the record or disclose current correctness.

Only a complete valid input updates BEST. Off-mark, zero or lost grasp makes READY invalid while BEST remains. New stable configurations are evaluated automatically, including intermediate configurations during movement; bind a record change to an actually observed configuration, not an assumed target.

L2/L3 require a separate robot to hold each blue handle with the whole module at least 20 mm clear of external supports. Maintain that support during red operation. A crank grip moves around the axle and may require coordinated translation.
Unlock occurs only when all digits of one simultaneous valid input are correct. Success latches, while physical springs and support remain active. Inputs and actuation choices are Agent decisions.
Only robot actuators and real contacts may affect the live world. Use RGB and permitted robot feedback; hidden passwords, per-dial correctness and live object truth are not policy inputs.
